full_judgment: 2. The petitioners challenged the validity of keeping under acquisition unutilised lands by the requiring body long after the completion of the project for which they were acquired. The facts as stated in the petition are, in short, that the lands appertaining to CS plot Nos. 394 and 113 and 92 of Mouza Kafrul. PS Dhaka Cantonment, measuring an area of 28.23 acres of land belonged to the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners, out of which the then Government of East Pakistan acquired 22.88 acres of land comprising CS Plot Nos. 1, 32, 34, 35, 36, 55, 56, 57 and 81 of Mouza Kafrul for expansion and development of the old Tejgaon Airport under LA Case Nos. 16/58-59. 7/60-61. 186/62-63,43/64-65 and 43/65-66. Partial compensation was given to the petitioners for the lands thus acquired under the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948. The expansion and development of the said Airport were completed in course of time but an area of 17.35 acres appertaining to Khatian Nos. 394, 113 and 92 of Mouza Kafrul remained unutilised, of which the petitioners claim to own an area 2,6097 acres. They also claim to be in possession of the lands by constructing homestead, sheds and structures and by exercising acts of right, title, interest and possession. The petitioners further state that since requisition and acquisition in 1958-59 long 35 years have lapsed but these lands have not yet been used by the requiring body for the purpose of expansion and development of the old Tejgaon Airport.
